title: Broad-Spectrum Multi-Epitope Design Targeting Conserved Hantavirus Glycoproteins (Gn/Gc): Chimeric Antigen Engineering and Structural Mapping

analysis.research_question_and_background: Hantaviruses cause severe zoonotic diseases such as hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) and hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS), yet no FDA-approved vaccine exists. analysis.methods: Predicted epitopes were evaluated for allergenicity, toxicity, conservation, and population coverage. title: A streamlined visual RT-RAA-CRISPR/Cas12a assay for rapid detection of Schmallenberg virus

analysis.research_question_and_background: Schmallenberg virus (SBV) causes febrile illness, reduced milk production in adult ruminants, and congenital malformations in fetuses, posing a substantial global threat to livestock health. Rapid, field-adaptable diagnostic approaches are urgently needed to address this emerging arboviral disease.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study developed a visual nucleic acid detection assay for SBV by combining reverse transcription recombinase-aided amplification (RT-RAA) with the CRISPR/Cas12a system, targeting conserved regions of the SBV S gene. Sensitivity was determined as 8.6 copies/μL for the SBV-S plasmid and 8.6 × 10^1 copies/μL for RNA transcripts. Specificity was assessed against a panel including Seoul orthohantavirus (SEOV), infectious bovine rhinotracheitis virus (IBRV), Rift Valley fever virus (RVFV), Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever virus (CCHFV), and bovine viral diarrhea virus (BVDV), with no cross-reactivity observed.
analysis.main_results: The assay achieved a sensitivity of 8.6 copies/μL for the SBV-S plasmid and 8.6 × 10^1 copies/μL for RNA transcripts, with no cross-reactivity against the tested panel of pathogens. In simulated clinical samples, the assay's sensitivity exceeded that of conventional RT-qPCR.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the assay as demonstrating favorable analytical performance for SBV detection, highlighting its single closed-tube format that reduces cross-contamination risk.
